Understanding Cooled and Uncooled Surveillance Cameras

Home » News » Understanding Cooled and Uncooled Surveillance Cameras

  • April 25, 2025

How to Select the Best Surveillance Camera for Your Security Needs

Surveillance technology is critical in securing borders, perimeters, and other vital areas, particularly under low-light or nighttime conditions. Among the options available, thermal imaging cameras are a standout choice for their ability to detect objects and individuals regardless of lighting conditions. Within this category, a significant decision lies in choosing between cooled and uncooled thermal cameras.

This article explores the core differences between these two technologies, outlining their strengths, weaknesses, and ideal use cases.

Cooled Thermal Cameras

Cooled thermal cameras are equipped with advanced sensors integrated with a cryocooler. This cooling device lowers the sensor’s temperature to cryogenic levels, reducing thermally induced noise and allowing the camera to detect even the smallest temperature differences.

Key Features of Cooled Cameras

  • High Sensitivity: Exceptional ability to detect subtle temperature differences, crucial for identifying small or distant targets.
  • Spectral Filtering: Cooled cameras excel in applications requiring precise filtering, such as imaging through smoke, flame, or other obscurants.
  • Long-Range Detection: These cameras often feature mid-wave infrared (MWIR) sensors, which provide higher thermal contrast for detailed imaging at extended distances.
  • High-Speed Imaging: Cooled cameras can precisely capture fast-moving objects due to their superior frame rates and low thermal lag.

Challenges of Cooled Cameras

  • Higher Costs: The cryocooler adds significant cost to the camera in terms of upfront expense and maintenance.
  • Maintenance Requirements: Cryocoolers require periodic servicing, usually every 8,000–10,000 hours of operation, increasing the total cost of ownership.

Uncooled Thermal Cameras

Uncooled cameras operate without cryogenic cooling. Instead, they use microbolometer sensors that detect infrared radiation emitted by objects. These cameras are often used for general-purpose thermal imaging and are popular due to their affordability and reliability.

Key Features of Uncooled Cameras

  • Cost-Effective: Uncooled cameras are generally less expensive to manufacture and maintain than their cooled counterparts.
  • Durability: With fewer moving parts, these cameras can operate continuously for years without requiring extensive servicing.
  • Ease of Use: Their simpler design makes them suitable for a wide range of applications, including security and surveillance in urban or moderate climates.
  • Good Performance in Fog: Uncooled cameras operating in the long-wave infrared (LWIR) spectrum perform better than MWIR sensors in foggy conditions.

Challenges of Uncooled Cameras

  • Lower Sensitivity: Compared to cooled cameras, uncooled sensors are less effective at detecting minute temperature differences.
  • Limited Spectral Flexibility: They lack the spectral filtering capabilities of cooled cameras, making them less suitable for specialized applications.

Choosing Between Cooled and Uncooled Cameras

The choice between cooled and uncooled cameras depends mainly on the specific surveillance requirements:

Use Cooled Cameras when high sensitivity, long-range detection, and specialized imaging capabilities are essential, such as in border surveillance, military applications, or industrial monitoring.

Use Uncooled Cameras for general surveillance, cost-sensitive projects, and applications where durability and continuous operation are critical.

Cooled and Uncooled Camera Solutions from MCA

As a platinum-level channel partner of Silent Sentinel and Motorola Solutions, MCA proudly offers an extensive range of cooled and uncooled thermal imaging solutions. Below are examples of the advanced technologies available through our partnerships.

Cooled Cameras from Silent Sentinel

Silent Sentinel provides state-of-the-art cooled cameras, such as their Medium-Wave Infrared (MWIR) Cooled Thermal Cameras. These systems utilize advanced cryogenic technology for high sensitivity and precision, enabling detection of small targets at extreme ranges.

Key features include:

  • High-Sensitivity Sensors: InSb MWIR focal plane arrays with resolutions of up to 640 x 512 pixels.
  • Exceptional Range: Lenses up to 960mm, enabling detection of human-sized targets at multi-kilometer distances.
  • Robust Design: Tested for performance in harsh environments, including extreme heat and cold.
  • Applications: Ideal for border surveillance, maritime security, and critical infrastructure protection.

Osiris Cooled MWIR Cameras

  • Lens options: 68.7–550mm, 43.6–785mm, 75–900mm, and 55.5–1000mm.
  • Features: High-definition (HD) cooled mid-wave infrared sensors with 1280 x 1024 pixels resolutions and motorized optical zoom.
  • Applications: Border surveillance, maritime security, and industrial monitoring.

Jaegar Cooled MWIR Cameras

  • Lens options: 16.6–300mm, 30.5–550mm, and 43.6–785mm.
  • Features: Motorized zoom lenses, ruggedized housing (IP67), and exceptional range performance.
  • Applications: Critical infrastructure protection, perimeter surveillance, and environmental monitoring.

Aeron Cooled MWIR Cameras

  • Lens options: 43.6–785mm.
  • Features: Compact and ruggedized platform, optimized for rapid deployment.
  • Applications: Police operations, remote monitoring, and emergency response.

Uncooled Cameras from Silent Sentinel

Silent Sentinel’s Advanced Uncooled Thermal Cameras bridge the gap between performance and cost-efficiency. These systems are designed to provide high sensitivity while minimizing lifetime ownership costs.

Key features include:

  • Optimized for Long-Term Use: No cryocooler servicing required, ensuring uninterrupted operation.
  • Thermal Video Stabilization: Maintains image clarity during movement or environmental disturbances.
  • Wide Lens Options: Fixed and zoom lenses up to 300mm are available, and they are suitable for mid-to-long-range applications.
  • Applications: Perfect for perimeter security, wildlife monitoring, and urban surveillance.

Aeron Ranger LR

  • Lens options: 15–75mm and 25–150mm.
  • Features: 12-micron pixel pitch, fast thermal autofocus, and electronic image stabilization.
  • Applications: Vehicle-mounted surveillance, perimeter security, and urban monitoring.

Osiris Ranger LR

  • Lens options: 25–150mm and 25–225mm.
  • Features: Compact and rugged housing, continuous zoom optics, and video stabilization.
  • Applications: Airport surveillance, coastal monitoring, and public safety.

Jaegar Ranger LR

  • Lens options: 25–150mm, 25–225mm, and 40–300mm.
  • Features: Advanced uncooled LWIR sensors, long-range capabilities, and optimized contrast for humid or foggy conditions.
  • Applications: Border security, maritime monitoring, and critical asset protection.

LR Series Cameras
